question: The British Government passed a law in the year 1856. It was meant for which among the following social reforms?

options.text: Abolition of Practice of Child Marriage
Law against Murdering of Female Child
Abolition of the Practice of Sati

solution:
The correct answer is __**Widow Remarriage**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The British Government passed the Widow Remarriage Act in 1856.
 
• This act was a significant social reform aimed at improving the condition of widows in India.
 
• It allowed Hindu widows to remarry, which was previously prohibited by societal norms and religious practices.
 
• The act was championed by social reformers like Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, who worked tirelessly to advocate for the rights of widows.
 
• The enactment of this law marked a progressive step towards gender equality and social justice in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Widow Remarriage Act of 1856 is also known as Act XV of 1856.
 
• This law was enacted during the tenure of Lord Dalhousie, the then Governor-General of India.
 
• The act was a result of the growing influence of the British colonial administration and reformist movements within Indian society.
 
• It played a crucial role in challenging the orthodox Hindu customs and paved the way for further social reforms in the country.
 
• Despite its enactment, widow remarriage faced significant resistance and took time to become widely accepted in society.
